title: TUI viewport, scroll, and performance gates
objective: Add regression gates that prove the new TUI substrate behaves correctly across desktop-sized, narrow, short, and long-session terminal scenarios.
actions: Add viewport regression cases for narrow, short, normal, and tall terminal dimensions.
Add long-session transcript tests for 1000+ messages, streaming appends, scroll-away, search, and expansion.
Add a lightweight performance benchmark or smoke gate for render count, append cost, and memory growth.
Verify overlay/modal/input/footer combinations do not overlap or steal rows unexpectedly.
Document the TUI architecture boundary and performance assumptions after implementation.

criteria: Viewport tests cover short, narrow, normal, and long-session layouts.
Performance gate fails on obvious full-transcript remount regressions.
Search, jump-to-bottom, sticky prompt, overlay, and footer navigation have regression coverage.
Docs describe the renderer substrate and the fallback path clearly.
`npm run check` and the targeted TUI test suite pass.

verification: node --import tsx --test src/tui/conversation-render.test.ts src/tui/conversation-layout.test.ts src/tui/chat-input-controller.test.ts src/tui/input-rendering.test.ts src/tui/tui-performance.test.ts
non_goals: Do not require external terminals or manual screenshots for the core regression gate.
Do not make benchmark thresholds so strict that normal CI variance fails builds.
Do not expand docs beyond the verified TUI architecture.
findings: Added viewport gates for short, narrow, normal, and tall terminal budgets without requiring external terminal screenshots.
Added long-session gates for 1200-1500 message transcripts, append cache reuse, offscreen search jump behavior, mounted message bounds, and expanded fold height/cache isolation.
Added a lightweight `src/bench/tui-long-session.ts` smoke benchmark that reports initial render, append render, mounted message counts, and append cache hit/miss counts.
Updated docs to describe the incremental Ink ScrollBox/virtual transcript renderer substrate and its verified performance assumptions.
